title: Buster the hamster home safe after hitching ride in Halloween pumpkin
summary: A adventurous hamster named Buster is back home in Arnprior, Ont., three weeks after hitching a ride inside a discarded Halloween pumpkin and ending up on a farm about 20 kilometres away.

image.caption: Covered in orange pumpkin juice, one family’s pet hamster, Buster, turned up inside a donated pumpkin that was left for over 21 days. (Castlegarth Farms/Facebook)

blocks.text: Ottawa·New
A adventurous hamster named Buster is back home in Arnprior, Ont., three weeks after hitching a ride inside a discarded Halloween pumpkin and ending up on a farm about 20 kilometres away.
Couple found Arnprior family's pet on their farm 3 weeks later and 20 km away
· CBC News
· Posted: Nov 25, 2026 3:39 PM EST | Last Updated: 8 minutes ago
Every November, Matthew Brearley and Tanya Sprowl collect donated pumpkins at Castlegarth Farms in White Lake, Ont., where they're used for compost.
The couple told CBC’s Ottawa Morning that they typically inspect the pumpkins for non-compostable items such as forgotten tea lights.

"We go through each pumpkin, piling it on the compost pile, and there was quite a sizable amount," Brearly said. "I was turning it over, looked down and saw what I thought was not a hamster, but [another kind of] small rodent, which does happen on farms."
But after a closer look, Brearley realized this was no typical farmyard rodent, but a domesticated hamster that's definitely not native to the Ottawa Valley.
Buster had spent an estimated 21 days inside the pumpkin, where he at least had plenty to eat.
"He was quite wet, he was covered in pumpkin guts and juice," said Sprowl. "So he was a little scraggly, but he seemed otherwise OK and didn’t have any injuries."
'That's Buster!'

Brearley scooped the hamster up and brought him into the house to be properly fed and cleaned. Figuring he was someone's missing pet, the couple took Buster's "mug shot" and posted it to a local Facebook group in an attempt to find his owners.

"He must have crawled into one of their Halloween pumpkins to have a snack and then ended up in the pile at the Nick Smith Centre bound for a dump truck that was headed to our farm for composting," the Facebook post read.
Word spread quickly.
"People followed the story all weekend looking for updates. It was kind of funny,” Brearley said.
Eventually, a family from Arnprior reached out.
"They sent us a direct message saying, 'That’s Buster!’ and they had been tearing their house apart for the last three weeks looking for their hamster," Sprowl said.
Sprowl said Buster was finally reunited with his owners after being "fluffed up" and made more presentable. Buster's family, which includes three boys, declined to comment for this story.
Brearley said it was an unexpectedly happy ending to a remarkable adventure.
"I would’ve been surprised if my hamster disappeared three weeks ago. I would’ve assumed it gone forever, but there it was, no foul and reunited with its family,” he said.
"He’s one lucky hamster that’s for sure,” the couple wrote on Facebook, thanking the online community for helping make Buster's homecoming happen.
